faq_heading: Government Road condos and townhomes: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Government Road. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Government Road, Burnaby: 23 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September 2026 and 3 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 13%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. By listings that is number 9 of 35 Burnaby communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Burnaby total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in Government Road fell from 26 in June to 23 in September (−11.5%), and 20 sold across the 4 months. In September the community held 1.7% of Burnaby’s 1,333 condos and townhomes listed.

blocks.text: Government Road home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

39 condos sold in Government Road with a median price of $505,000 (the middle half sold between $472,500 and $560,400), taking a median of 22 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 5% sold above list. They had a median $567 per square foot, a median year built of 1983 and a median strata fee of $475 a month. 13 townhomes sold in Government Road with a median price of $999,900 (the middle half sold between $900,000 and $1,035,000), taking a median of 14 days to sell at 97.3% of the last list price; 15% sold above list. They had a median $652 per square foot, a median year built of 2007 and a median strata fee of $445 a month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Government Road
Sandlewood — 9233 + 9283 Government Street
Polygon's wood-frame low-rise, built 2007 — the corridor's newest condo stock. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
Concorde Place — 9521 Cardston Court

A concrete building, built 1983; a current listing title gives "211 Unit Development, Concrete." That listing's headline reads "No Pets or Rentals" — the rentals half is void, and the building directory itself records pets not allowed, rentals allowed. Some listings spell the name "Concord Place" — same building. Published building work: repiping, envelope, roof and elevators. (Headline spelling varies by listing; the directory name is Concorde Place.)
Discovery Place I — 3980 Carrigan Court

Built 1985. Published restrictions: pets not allowed, rentals allowed. Amenities: indoor pool, recreation centre, sauna, hot tub, squash. Note: its T-prefixed units (for example T4907) are marketed as "one-level townhomes" inside this tower complex — they are part of this complex, not a separate townhome development. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
Discovery Place II, marketed as The Harrington — 3970 Carrigan Court
It is counted once. Confirm name, year and pet position from the strata plan/Form B for the specific unit.
Lougheed Estates — 9202 Horne Street

Built 1974. Published restrictions: pets allowed with restrictions; rentals "allowed with restrictions" — the restriction element is void under current law. Amenities: indoor pool, recreation centre, sauna, hot tub; a current listing records elevators replaced in 2025. Naming is inconsistent in the market: some current listings label this address "Lougheed Estates II," which is also the directory name of the 3901 Carrigan Court building below — verify the strata plan, not the listing name. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
Lougheed Estates II — 3901 Carrigan Court
Built 1974, 102 units per the building directory. Amenities: indoor pool, hot tub, sauna, exercise room, workshop. Published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED in the sources checked.
Woodstone Place — 9101 Horne Street

A wood-frame low-rise; the majority of listings state built 1975 (one unit listing says 1976 — noted, not resolved). A current listing states "Pets and rentals allowed" and that the strata fee includes heat, hot water and the gas fireplace. Amenities: pool, sauna, jacuzzi, gym, woodworking shop. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
Streets, schools and getting around Government Road

items.t: Government Road is a residential/light-industrial corridor running south of Lougheed Highway, between the Lougheed Town Centre/Cameron lands to the east and Burnaby Lake/Sperling to the west. Government Road itself is the spine; the residential pocket hangs off it on Carrigan Court, Cardston Court and Horne Street.
Where the condo stock concentrates: that one pocket — seven complexes built 1974–2007, from 1970s low-rise and towers to a 2007 Polygon low-rise at the corridor's west end.

Schools: École Seaforth Elementary (7881 Government Road), Stoney Creek Community Elementary (2740 Beaverbrook Crescent), Cameron Elementary (9540 Erickson Drive) and Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8800 Eastlake Drive).
Transit: route 110 runs on Government Road itself (Lougheed Station ↔ Metrotown via Beaverbrook, Eastlake, Brighton, Phillips and Winston) — the corridor's own street carries the bus.
Green anchor: Stoney Creek Park and its trail system on the east side.

Planning frame: the Lochdale Urban Village Plan was adopted July 25, 2022 — it governs the lands north across Lougheed Highway, not this corridor's south side, but it is the document reshaping the corridor's northern edge.

blocks.text: Good to know about Government Road

items.t: Two of the seven complexes share one name, loosely. "Lougheed Estates" is the directory name at 9202 Horne Street and "Lougheed Estates II" at 3901 Carrigan Court — yet some current listings label the Horne Street building "Lougheed Estates II" as well. Document orders and depreciation reports run to the strata corporation; confirm the plan number before ordering anything.

The newest condos and the townhomes are one Polygon project area. Sandlewood (2007 condos) and Terramor (2007 townhomes) sit side by side on Government Street and share the club-amenity set in listings — but they are different strata product, and a search that merges 9133 and 9233 Government Street will mix them.
Zero detached sales is a recorded month here.

The plan reshaping the area stops at the highway. The Lochdale Urban Village Plan (adopted July 25, 2022) covers the lands north across Lougheed — the corridor's own south-side zoning story is the general Burnaby framework, so "Lochdale village" marketing for a south-side address should be read as proximity, not plan coverage.
Jared's own sold history in this sub-area is UNVERIFIED.

Streets, schools and getting around Government Road

items.t: Municipality: City of Burnaby, BC. Government Road is the residential and light-industrial corridor in north-east Burnaby running south of Lougheed Highway, between the Lougheed Town Centre / Cameron lands to the east and Burnaby Lake and the Sperling side to the west, named for Government Road and anchored by École Seaforth Elementary at 7881 Government Rd.

"Government Road" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby. Boundaries: UNVERIFIED — no City source read publishes street-by-street boundaries for the sub-area; the confirmed anchors are Government Road itself, Stoney Creek Community Elementary at 2740 Beaverbrook Cres on the east side, and Burnaby Lake Regional Park at the west and south-west side.
Nearby areas: Lougheed Town Centre and Cameron to the east, Cariboo to the south-east, Burnaby Lake to the west and south-west, Montecito and Lochdale to the north across Lougheed Highway.

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) has no middle-school tier — elementary is K–7 and secondary is 8–12. In-area schools on the Province's list are École Seaforth Elementary (K–7), 7881 Government Rd, and Stoney Creek Community Elementary (K–7), 2740 Beaverbrook Cres, with Cameron Elementary (K–7), 9540 Erickson Dr, and Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8–12), 8800 Eastlake Dr, on the east and north-east side.

Transit: route 110 is the area's spine bus — from Lougheed Station via Cameron, Beaverbrook, Eastlake, Production Way–University Station, Brighton, Government Road itself, Phillips and Winston to Sperling Station, then on to Metrotown Station. The Millennium Line stations serving the area are Lougheed Station and Production Way–University Station to the east and Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station to the west.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Government Road

items.t: City zoning frame: the governing bylaw is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815), adopted June 9, 2026 and in effect July 1, 2026 — never the repealed 1965 Zoning Bylaw No. 4742. Burnaby consolidated its former single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District in June 2024: R1 lots may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. The industrial and office parcels along the corridor are not R1 — confirm the zone parcel by parcel.

Form B diligence (both strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Directory and listing rental/pet lines in are secondary-source data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

Hazards: Stoney Creek runs through the area to Burnaby Lake and the lake's east shore is low and wet; a floodplain designation for Government Road's residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read, and parcel-level hazard, watercourse-setback and ALR status are property-specific checks — ALR status through the Agricultural Land Commission.

blocks.text: Good to know about Government Road

items.t: The governing zoning bylaw changed mid-2026. Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) took effect July 1, 2026 — any advice, listing copy or older page citing the 1965 Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 for a Government Road property is citing a repealed bylaw.

The plan across the highway is not this corridor's plan. The Lochdale Urban Village Community Plan (adopted July 25, 2022) covers the lands north across Lougheed Highway; Government Road parcels are governed by the Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) and the parcel's own zone.

The original Seaforth School is a 1922 heritage building — and it is not on Government Road anymore. The City's heritage record dates the original Seaforth School to 1922 and notes it has since been relocated to Burnaby Village Museum; the operating school at 7881 Government Rd is the modern École Seaforth Elementary.

Burnaby Lake is a working regional park, not just scenery: Metro Vancouver's Burnaby Lake Regional Park is a wildlife sanctuary with a rowing course, a rowing pavilion and public canoe launch at the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex, a Nature House, and viewing towers and docks — and the City and Metro Vancouver signed a 25-year lease in 2025 for the 360-acre park Metro Vancouver has managed since 1978.

Stoney Creek's park lands are dedicated by bylaw: the Stoney Creek Park and Trail System and the Cariboo and Brunette River Conservation Lands run through the area's east side, and Stoney Creek Park carries 2 tennis courts and 2 pickleball courts on the City's outdoor courts list — creek-edge lots carry watercourse setbacks that travel with the creek.

The area's hospital is across the city: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health), serves Burnaby from the west side — a Government Road buyer's hospital trip is a cross-city trip, not a neighbourhood one.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Government Road?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 23 condos and townhomes listed in Government Road. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Government Road a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Government Road had a sales ratio of 13%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Government Road from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 20 condos and townhomes sold in Government Road over those 4 months, out of 750 in all of Burnaby.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Government Road sell for?
faq.a: 39 condos sold in Government Road between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $505,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Government Road?
faq.a: The median was 22 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.1% of the last list price (5% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Are these buildings part of The City of Lougheed?
faq.a: No. The City of Lougheed towers stand north of Lougheed Highway; every complex in sits south of the highway in the Government Road corridor and is MLS-classified Government Road. The stock is also a different era — 1974–2007 low-rise and mid-rise, not new town-centre towers.

faq.q: What is the newest stock in the corridor?
faq.a: Polygon's 2007 pair at the west end: the Sandlewood condo low-rise (9233 + 9283 Government Street, wood-frame, Sandlewood Club amenities) and the Terramor townhomes next door at 9133 Government Street.

faq.q: A Concorde Place listing says "No Pets or Rentals" — is that enforceable?
faq.a: Half of it. The rentals half is void — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, and the building directory itself records rentals allowed. The pets half matches the directory (pets not allowed) and remains a live bylaw question for the Form B.

faq.q: Is 3970 Carrigan Court called Discovery Place II or The Harrington?
faq.a: It is one building, counted once in; order documents by the strata plan number, not the marketing name.

faq.q: How old is the oldest stock, and what has been done to it?
faq.a: Lougheed Estates (9202 Horne Street) and Lougheed Estates II (3901 Carrigan Court) both date to 1974. Published work includes elevators replaced in 2025 at 9202 Horne; the balance of the envelope/mechanical picture is a depreciation-report question — every strata here with 5+ lots has owed one every five years since July 1, 2024.

faq.q: Terramor shows two addresses and two build years — is it one complex?
faq.a: Yes, one complex counted once: the directory records it at 9088 Halston Court, built 2006, while listings at 9133 Government Street record built 2007. The year is UNCONFIRMED between 2006 and 2007; the strata plan and Form B settle it.

faq.q: Can I rent out my Government Road townhouse?
faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. Terramor's directory record reads "rentals allowed" in any case. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.

faq.q: Is Tudor Village really strata? It looks like garden apartments.
faq.a: The current listing data records a strata fee ($724/mo on MLS®) and an earlier listing records water and heat included in monthly fees — a strata-fee structure. No strata plan number was published in the sources read, so confirm the plan and the depreciation report on the Form B before subjects come off.
